key_insight: Four-tetrahedron macro-element condensation shrinks interior-point Newton systems, enabling faster and more memory-efficient 3D equilibrium-based plasticity solves.
engineering_relevance: The approach makes larger statically admissible elastoplasticity and limit-analysis computations feasible on CPUs and GPUs.
method: Eliminate stress directions and macro-internal traction-continuity multipliers to form reduced systems suitable for positive-definite factorization.
Establish global and macro-local nonsingularity conditions, using trace-bound augmentation for von Mises limit analysis.
Implement batched macro-local operations in CUDA Fortran and reduced sparse solves with cuDSS.
evidence_signal: Reported tests show up to approximately 2× CPU speedup and 66.5% lower peak linear-solver memory versus stress-only elimination; the GPU implementation reaches up to 13.5× speedup over its CPU counterpart and 87.5× over MOSEK.
watch_item: For elastoplasticity, the lower-memory GPU conjugate-gradient option increases solution time relative to the direct GPU solver.
paper_title: A GPU Interior-Point Solver with Macro-Element Condensation for Equilibrium-Based Plasticity
